name: canvas
description: Save and read rich content from Jarvis Canvas - a visual viewer for research results, code snippets, comparisons, and reference material. Use when: (1) user asks to research something and results are complex, (2) user explicitly asks to 'save to canvas' or 'put in viewer', (3) content has tables, code, or detailed formatting that benefits from visual display, (4) user asks 'what's on my canvas?' or 'read my canvas page about X'. Canvas shows Markdown beautifully with syntax highlighting. After saving, tell user 'I've put that in your canvas' so they know to look. Actions: create (new page), update (modify existing), delete (remove page), list (show all pages), open (get canvas URL), read (get page content - useful for verification, troubleshooting, or reading back).

action.description: Action to perform. create=new page, update=modify existing, delete=remove, list=show all, open=get URL, read=get page content

title.description: Page title (required for create, optional for update)

content.description: Markdown content for the page. Supports headers, lists, tables, code blocks with syntax highlighting.

tags.description: Tags for categorization. Examples: research, code, reference, movies, servers

source_query.description: The original user query that led to this content (for reference)

page_id.description: Page ID for update/delete/read actions. Format: page_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS

search.description: Search term to find pages by title or content (for read action). Example: 'bitcoin' finds pages mentioning bitcoin.

pinned.description: Pin page to top of list

limit.description: Max pages to return for list action (default 10)
